ask.text:
The rope bridge over the ravine to the far gardens is old, and the builders have been meaning to replace it for a year. This morning (name) steps onto it with a basket of seedlings and hears one of the ropes go "tick." Then another "tick." Then the bridge sags a hand's width.
(Name) is a third of the way across. Should (he/she) hurry forward to the far side, or edge carefully back the way (he/she) came?

c1o1.text: The bridge gives way just as (name) reaches the far side. (He/She) grabs the edge, scrambles up, and smacks (his/her) head against a rock doing it. The gardeners find (him/her) sitting dazed among the seedlings an hour later. (He/She) knows the gardens, the village and the gardeners, but not (his/her) own name. Until it comes back, everyone calls (him/her) "?", and the builders build a new bridge in a week.

c1o2.text: The bridge breaks under (name) with the far side almost in reach. (He/She) falls, hits the slope, and slides down into the ferns at the bottom of the ravine. It takes the whole afternoon to bring (him/her) up on a stretcher. (His/her) legs never work properly again, and (he/she) never goes near the far gardens after that. The builders build the new bridge in a week, out of guilt.

c1.text: (Name) runs, the bridge swinging wildly under (his/her) feet, seedlings flying out of the basket into the ravine. The ticks come faster and faster...

c2o1.text: (Name) reaches the near side just as the bridge drops. It hangs straight down from the far side, swinging. (Name) sits on the rock for a long time, holding the basket of seedlings. (He/She) never goes back to the far gardens, and the love (he/she) had for growing things seems to have fallen into the ravine with the bridge. "I'll do something on flat ground," (he/she) says.

c2o2.text: A builder on the near side sees what's happening and throws (name) a rope. (Name) ties it around (his/her) waist with shaking hands, and the builder hauls (him/her) back to safety as the old bridge sags and twists. The new bridge goes up that week. (Name) is the first to cross it, very slowly, holding both ropes.

c2.text: (Name) turns very, very slowly and starts edging back, one step at a time, holding both ropes. The bridge creaks. Halfway back, another rope goes "tick"...
